editorial:
Imagine being a straight-A student who suddenly gets thrown into a school that feels more like a prison. That is exactly what happens to the main lead when he transfers to Jungmoon High. You will quickly see that this place is no joke. The teachers are scary and use harsh punishments, while the students are split into violent gangs fighting for control. It is a wild mix of teenage rebellion, first loves, and chaotic fights. You get to see a funny and touching side to the characters, even the ones who seem like bullies at first, making the whole experience feel like a trip back to a rougher time in school.

The acting is great because the cast makes you really care about their friendships and struggles. The fight scenes are exciting, and the pacing keeps you interested without feeling too slow. While some of the drama feels a bit over the top, it adds to the charm of the movie. If you love stories about underdogs and school wars, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: At the end, the cycle of violence finally breaks as the students realize that fighting each other does not solve anything. The main characters grow up and move past their school rivalries. It wraps up with a bittersweet feeling, showing that while they survived the madness of Jungmoon High, the experience changed them forever. You see them reflecting on their youth, proving that friendship was the only thing that actually mattered in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high school dramas and fight movies.
